nl.statement: A finite latent-shift structural causal model. The state spaces \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\) are finite, with \(\mathcal E,\mathcal X\) nonempty, \(2\le r=\lvert\mathcal U\rvert\), \(m=\lvert\mathcal W\rvert\ge r\) and \(\lvert\mathcal Y\rvert\ge2\). The known causal graph \(\mathcal G\) on \((E,U,W,X,Y)\) has arrows \(E\to U\), \(U\to W\), \(U\to X\), \(U\to Y\), \(W\to Y\), \(X\to Y\). A model \(\mathcal M=(\pi,S,M,a,f,q)\) consists of a strictly positive environment law \(\pi\in\Delta^{\circ}(\mathcal E)\), a strictly positive column-stochastic latent channel \(S\in\mathbb R^{r\times\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}\) with \(S_{ue}=P(U=u\mid E=e)\), a strictly positive column-stochastic proxy channel \(M\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\) with \(M_{wu}=P(W=w\mid U=u)\), a strictly positive treatment kernel \(a_x(u)=P(X=x\mid U=u)\), a strictly positive outcome kernel \(f_{x,y}(u,w)=P(Y=y\mid U=u,W=w,X=x)\), and a strictly positive target latent mixture \(q\in\Delta^{\circ}(\mathcal U)\); it induces the source full-data law \(P_{\mathcal M}\) on \(\mathcal E\times\mathcal U\times\mathcal W\times\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\) and the target law \(Q_{\mathcal M}\) on \(\mathcal U\times\mathcal W\times\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\), Markov relative to \(\mathcal G\). All six primitives are normalized -- \(\sum_e\pi_e=1\), \(\sum_uS_{ue}=1\), \(\sum_wM_{wu}=1\), \(\sum_xa_x(u)=1\), \(\sum_yf_{x,y}(u,w)=1\), \(\sum_uq_u=1\) -- and \(P_{\mathcal M}\), \(Q_{\mathcal M}\) are probability laws on their product spaces, so the observed law \(P_O\) and the target proxy law \(b\) below are themselves probability distributions on \(\mathcal E\times\mathcal W\times\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\) and on \(\mathcal W\). Writing \(\mathfrak M_{+}\) for the class of such models with \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=r\), the observed data are \(\mathcal D=(P_O,b)\) with \(P_O(e,w,x,y)=\sum_uP_{\mathcal M}(e,u,w,x,y)\) and \(b_w=Q_{\mathcal M}(W=w)\); the derived quantities are \(\rho_x(e)=P_O(X=x\mid E=e)\), \(R_x(u,e)=a_x(u)S_{ue}/\rho_x(e)\), \(B_x(w,e)=P_O(W=w\mid E=e,X=x)\), \(c_{x,y}(e)=P_O(Y=y\mid E=e,X=x)\), \(g_{x,y}(u)=\sum_wM_{wu}f_{x,y}(u,w)\), the unconditional moments \(H_x(w,e)=P_O(E=e,W=w,X=x)\) and \(z_{x,y}(e)=P_O(E=e,X=x,Y=y)\), and the causal query \(\theta_{x,y}=Q_{\mathcal M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))\), obtained from \(Q_{\mathcal M}\) by deleting the treatment mechanism at the fixed value \(x\). Independent two-sample multinomial sampling from a fixed model in the class above, at a fixed error level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). nl.frozen_body:
The row models \((\mathcal M_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\) are normalized finite latent-shift SCMs on the finite state spaces \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\). For row \(n\), the observed source law \(P_{O,n}\) is defined by
\[
P_{O,n}(e,w,x,y)
=
\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}
P_{\mathcal M_n}(E=e,U=u,W=w,X=x,Y=y),
\]
and, writing \(M_n\) for the row proxy channel and \(q_n\) for the row target latent-state probability mass function, the target proxy law \(b_n\) is defined by
\[
b_n(w)=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U} M_n(w,u)q_n(u),
\qquad w\in\mathcal W.
\]
For sample sizes \(n_s,n_t\), the finite two-sample product sample space, with its discrete full power-set sigma-field, is
\[
\Omega(n_s,n_t)
=
(\mathcal E\times\mathcal W\times\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y)^{n_s}
\times
\mathcal W^{n_t},
\]
with
\[
\Omega_n=\Omega(n_s(n),n_t(n)).
\]
For every \(n\ge 2\), the finite row law on \(\Omega_n\) is
\[
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
=
P_{O,n}^{\otimes n_s(n)}\otimes b_n^{\otimes n_t(n)}.
\]
The source observations \((O^s_{1,n},\ldots,O^s_{n_s(n),n})\) are the source coordinate block under this law, and their marginal law is
\[
(\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)})\circ
(O^s_{1,n},\ldots,O^s_{n_s(n),n})^{-1}
=
P_{O,n}^{\otimes n_s(n)}.
\]

review.note: The row-law equality is exactly the stated source-target product law, and the additional source-block marginal equality follows from that equality via twoSampleLaw_sourceBlock, so it adds no restriction.
